items.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020
items.q: I think I would probably throw Metheny and Stan Getz in there [among the 50 most important jazz musicians]

ctx.x: Okay. How does it matter in your eyes?

How does it matter in my eyes? Well that’s too big a question to answer, God, how do you even begin? See since I was very young I loved black music. There were — radio was entirely segregated. There were white stations and black stations. The black ones were KDIA and KSOL. And I started listening to that. It was a revelation. It wasn’t something that most people in my circle would have ever listened to. I was asked to join a sort of rainbow soul band with — to be the saxophonist in a group that was Korean,…

role. This is functional music, this is culture, this is social interrelationships. And to see that was just an eye opening experience for an 18-year-old kid who grew up in Jewish culture you know. It was fantastic. And I think there are many other anecdotal instant answers like that of just experiencing life in ways in which musics of African-American origin had a cultural meaning that I didn’t find elsewhere. It wasn’t a split between music and life. I think another component of the answer that can go down a…
